newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Most Budapest grains futures limit-down on Chicago.
newsitem.headline: Most Budapest grains futures limit-down on Chicago.

text.p: Most grains futures contracts on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) went limit-down on Friday following Chicago price movements, traders said.
"Wheat prices dropped the equivalent of 800 forints on Thursday in Chicago so we could not entirely follow that," said Istvan Grebats of brokerage Termin.
On the BCE, price movements are limited to 400 forints per day.
All milling wheat positions dropped 400 forints per tonne to end at between 21,610 forints for July and 25,600 for May.
Grebats added that although milling wheat prices could continue their downward movement, prices were unlikely to fall below 21,000 forints.
Feed wheat and barley followed milling wheat, losing 400 forints each, but in maize only July lost 400 forints.
"Producers appeared on the market and there were actual deals even at these low prices," Grebats said.
Other maize positions finished 150 to 290 forints lower in moderate turnover apart from May which was steady at 23,000 forints.
Maize turnover remained relatively low as the market has little information to trade on and the harvest is still too far away for reliable crop forecasts, traders said.
Total grains futures turnover was 823 lots or 350.43 million forints, up from Thursday's 696 lots or 311.5 million forints.
